First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1-\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{2\text{i}}{1+\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}(1-\text{i})}{(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}-2{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}+2}{1+1} \\  & =1+\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=1+\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=1$ and $y=1$ are both positive, $z$ lies in the first quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))
$$
